sources.entry: Hopp - Remote pair programming app with low-latency 4K screen sharing, drawing, and remote control, with clients for macOS and Windows (alternative to Tuple, Pop, Drovio, Coscreen). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Hopp is an open source screen sharing and remote pair programming app for developers, with low-latency screen sharing, drawing, and remote control, and an option to self-host its backend.
summary.what_it_does: Hopp is a desktop app for pair programming and screen sharing, built with Tauri and Rust on the client side, with WebRTC infrastructure provided by LiveKit. The README says it targets sub-100ms latency and supports mob programming with up to 10 people in a room. Users can pick a managed cloud backend at gethopp.app or run their own backend using the Docker Compose stack in the selfhost/ directory, which includes Postgres, Redis, LiveKit, and Caddy for automatic TLS. The repo is split into a desktop shell (tauri/), a screen capture and WebRTC engine (core/, Rust), a Go API server (backend/), a React/Vite web dashboard (web-app/), a dev LiveKit config, and the self-host stack. The README describes the app as offering one-click pairing to a teammate without sharing links.
use_cases: remote pair programming with a teammate
mob programming with up to 10 people
self-hosting a team screen sharing backend
low-latency remote control of a colleague's desktop
drawing on a shared screen during a call
how_to_run: See selfhost/README.md for localhost setup and docs.gethopp.app/open-source/self-hosting for the full guide
Download the desktop app for macOS (stable) or Windows (alpha)
notable: Open source alternative to Tuple, positioned for developers doing remote pair programming
Self-host stack with Docker Compose including Postgres, Redis, LiveKit, and Caddy auto-TLS
Built on Tauri and Rust for native desktop performance with low CPU overhead, per the README
Managed cloud option funds ongoing development of the OSS app
caveats: Windows client is alpha and Linux is only planned; macOS is the stable client
Managed cloud plan is paid after a 14-day free trial
Roadmap lists items still open, including Linux support, full Windows support, key bindings, and adaptive streaming resolution
keywords: share my screen with a teammate
